posts.text: If I make a programming error, the program usually either doesn't execute or the mistakes are super obvious. With coding agents, you'll encounter cases where the program works but took shortcuts/is subtly wrong. Opus was also stubborn about acknowledging bugs it introduced.
posts.summary: AI agents produce subtle errors, less transparent than traditional debugging

posts.text: You notice this more, too, if you have programming tasks that require extreme precision. Like, for our sports/election models, a forecast being off by a few percentage points is a fairly big deal (especially if people are comparing your numbers to e.g. prediction markets).
